title: Slope
note: Two points: \((x_1,y_1)\), \((x_2,y_2)\). If \(x_1=x_2\), slope is undefined.

title: Slope-intercept form
note: \(m\) = slope; \(b\) = y-intercept.

title: Midpoint
note: Average the two x-values and the two y-values.

title: Distance between two points
note: \(d\) = distance; keep subtraction order consistent.

title: Quadratic formula
note: For \(ax^2+bx+c=0\), with \(a\ne0\).

title: Mean
note: \(n\) = number of values, including repeats; \(n>0\).

title: Average speed
note: \(d\) = distance; \(t\) = time, greater than zero.

title: Probability of an event
note: Outcomes must be equally likely.

title: Both independent events
note: Only when A and B are independent.

title: Counting choices
note: \(n_i\) = choices at step i, when every choice allows the next choices.

title: Find p% of a number
note: \(p\) is the percent, such as 25 for 25%.

title: What percent is the part?
note: The whole must be nonzero.

title: Find the whole from a percent
Percent change
note: Positive original: increase is positive; decrease is negative.

title: Rectangle area
note: \(l\) = length; \(w\) = width.

title: Rectangle perimeter
note: \(l\) = length; \(w\) = width.

title: Rectangular prism volume
note: \(l\) = length; \(w\) = width; \(h\) = height.

title: Parallelogram area
note: \(b\) = base; \(h\) = perpendicular height.

title: Triangle area
note: \(b\) = base; \(h\) = perpendicular height.

title: Pythagorean theorem
note: Right triangle: \(a,b\) = legs; \(c\) = hypotenuse.

title: 45°–45°–90° triangle sides
note: Two equal legs, then hypotenuse; \(x>0\).

title: 30°–60°–90° triangle sides
note: Opposite 30°, 60°, then 90°; \(x>0\).

title: Trapezoid area
note: \(b_1,b_2\) = parallel bases; \(h\) = perpendicular height.

title: Circle area
note: \(r\) = radius.

title: Circle circumference
note: \(r\) = radius; \(d=2r\) = diameter.

title: Sector area
note: \(\theta\) = central angle in degrees; \(r\) = radius.

title: Arc length
note: \(\theta\) = central angle in degrees; \(r\) = radius.

title: Equation of a circle
note: Center \((h,k)\); radius \(r>0\).

title: Cylinder volume
note: \(r\) = base radius; \(h\) = perpendicular height.

title: Sine, cosine, tangent
note: Right triangle: O = opposite, A = adjacent, H = hypotenuse, relative to θ.

title: Reciprocal trig functions
note: Each reciprocal requires a defined, nonzero denominator.

title: Pythagorean trig identity
note: \(\sin^2\theta\) means \((\sin\theta)^2\).

title: Tangent in terms of sine and cosine
note: \(\cos\theta\ne0\).

title: Sine double-angle identity
note: Doubling the angle is different from squaring sine: \(\sin(2\theta)\ne\sin^2\theta\) in general.

title: Cosine double-angle identities
note: Choose the version using the trig value you know.

title: Tangent double-angle identity
note: Use where \(\tan\theta\) is defined and \(1-\tan^2\theta\ne0\).

title: Sine of an angle sum or difference
note: Sine keeps the chosen sign. Expand a sum or a difference, not the product of two angles.

title: Cosine of an angle sum or difference
note: Cosine uses the opposite sign: plus inside means minus outside.

title: Tangent of an angle sum or difference
note: The denominator uses the opposite sign. Both tangents and the result must be defined; the denominator cannot be zero.

title: Sine half-angle identity
note: Choose the sign using the quadrant of \(\theta/2\), not the quadrant of \(\theta\).

title: Cosine half-angle identity
note: Choose the sign using the quadrant of \(\theta/2\).

title: Tangent half-angle identity
note: Each fraction is usable only where its own denominator is nonzero and tangent is defined.

title: Squared sine and cosine identities
note: These rewrite a squared trig value using a double angle.

title: Pythagorean identities with secant and cosecant
note: First line requires \(\cos\theta\ne0\); second requires \(\sin\theta\ne0\).

title: Complementary-angle identities
note: In radians, replace \(90^\circ\) with \(\pi/2\). Use each identity where both sides are defined.

title: Negative-angle identities
note: Cosine is even. Sine and tangent are odd; tangent must be defined.

title: Unit-circle coordinates
note: On the circle of radius 1 centered at the origin. Tangent is \(y/x\) when \(x\ne0\).

title: Exact values at 30°
note: \(30^\circ=\pi/6\) radians.

title: Exact values at 45°
note: \(45^\circ=\pi/4\) radians.

title: Exact values at 60°
note: \(60^\circ=\pi/3\) radians.

title: Trig signs by quadrant
note: Use the reference angle for the size and the quadrant for the sign. Axis angles need separate evaluation.

title: Degrees and radians
note: One full turn is \(360^\circ=2\pi\) radians. Match your calculator’s angle mode.

title: Sine and cosine graph formulas
note: Also applies to cosine, with \(A,B\ne0\) and radians. Midline is \(y=D\); range is \([D-|A|,D+|A|]\).

title: Tangent graph period
note: \(A,B\ne0\), x in radians. Tangent has no finite amplitude. Its undefined inputs produce vertical asymptotes.

title: Law of sines
note: In a nondegenerate triangle, side a is opposite angle A, and likewise for b and c. SSA information can give two possible triangles.

title: Law of cosines
note: C is the included angle between sides a and b, opposite side c. Works for non-right triangles too.

title: Triangle area using an included angle
note: a and b are the two given sides; C is the angle between them.

title: Triangle angle sum
note: Interior angles of any plane triangle. An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

title: Triangle side inequality
note: Positive side lengths of a nondegenerate triangle. Equality would flatten the triangle.

title: Equilateral triangle area and height
note: All three sides have length s. Height h is perpendicular to the base.

title: Heron’s formula
note: a, b, c must form a valid triangle. Here s is the semiperimeter, not a side.

title: Polygon angle formulas
note: n ≥ 3 sides. Interior sum assumes a simple polygon; per-angle formulas assume a regular convex polygon.

title: Similar-figure scale factors
note: k > 0 is a corresponding length scale factor. K is area; V is volume. The whole figures must be similar.

title: Regular polygon area
note: a = apothem (center-to-side perpendicular distance); p = perimeter. The polygon must be regular.

title: Rectangular prism surface area
note: l = length, w = width, h = height. Includes all six faces of a closed box.

title: Cylinder surface area
note: Closed right circular cylinder: r = radius; h = perpendicular height. Two bases plus the curved side.

title: Cone volume
note: r = base radius; h = perpendicular height. Do not use slant height for volume.

title: Cone surface area
note: Closed right circular cone. ℓ = slant height; h = perpendicular height; r = radius. Lateral area alone is πrℓ.

title: Pyramid volume
note: B = base area, not base side length; h = perpendicular height.

title: Sphere volume
note: r = radius. A hemisphere has half this volume.

title: Sphere surface area
note: r = radius. A hemisphere’s curved area is half; add its circular base if the solid is closed.

title: Arc length and sector area in radians
note: θ is the nonnegative central angle in radians; r = radius; s = arc length; K = sector area.

title: Inscribed angle and intercepted arc
note: α is an inscribed angle; β is the measure of its intercepted arc in the same angle units. An angle subtending a diameter is 90°.

title: Intersecting chord lengths
note: Chords AB and CD intersect inside the circle at P. Multiply the two parts of each chord.

title: Tangent and secant lengths
note: From the same exterior point: t = tangent length; e = outside secant part; i = inside secant part.

title: Rotations about the origin
note: CW = clockwise; CCW = counterclockwise. These rules assume the origin is the center.

title: Coordinate reflections
note: Reflection flips a point across the named line. Distances and angle sizes stay the same.
